Their stated main theorems concern proportional-dimensional asymptotic equivalents, whereas this claim is a fixed-d exact gradient-conditioned inverse-step tail and moment law. The random-subspace source frameworks prove safeguarding/global complexity or asymptotic equivalent pseudoinverses. The first-order Haar second-moment computation has a different update without the singular projected inverse; it does not imply the exact inverse step-moment phase split.

value.rationale: A natural singular Gauss--Newton normal matrix has a consistent gradient in its range, but numerical/model mismatch adds a kernel component. At codimensions three or four this arbitrarily small mismatch turns a finite mean-square unrestricted reduced step into an infinite one, even while the compressed Hessian is positive definite almost surely. The sharp codimension and ridge laws inform modeling safeguards without asserting algorithmic divergence.
